questionText:

"The cotton textile industry is one of the oldest and most geographically widespread organized manufacturing sectors in India. The first modern mechanized cotton mill was set up at Fort Gloster near Kolkata in 1818, though the first commercially successful mill was established by C.N. Davar in Mumbai in 1854. Initially, the industry was concentrated heavily in Mumbai and Ahmedabad in the black soil (regur) cotton tract of Maharashtra and Gujarat, benefiting from local raw cotton, humid maritime climate preventing yarn snapping, access to Mumbai Port for machinery imports, and ready capital. Over time, the industry underwent profound spatial decentralization. Because cotton is a pure raw material that does not lose weight during spinning, mills can be located near consumer markets without incurring heavy freight penalties. "The cotton textile industry is one of the oldest and most geographically widespread organized manufacturing sectors in India. The first modern mechanized cotton mill was set up at Fort Gloster near Kolkata in 1818, though the first commercially successful mill was established by C.N. Davar in Mumbai in 1854. Initially, the industry was concentrated heavily in Mumbai and Ahmedabad in the black soil (regur) cotton tract of Maharashtra and Gujarat, benefiting from local raw cotton, humid maritime climate preventing yarn snapping, access to Mumbai Port for machinery imports, and ready capital. Because cotton is a pure raw material that does not lose weight during spinning, mills can be located near consumer markets without incurring heavy freight penalties.
